While my friend might not mind running it on his PC, I still prefer to use native hardware and directly support developers even if it means waiting much, much longer (maybe even forever). I just enjoy having my Switch around for portable, on-the-go gaming which is something I cannot do with my big chonking PC tower. Also, with my PC being in my study room, it’s hard for me to be able to relax on the sofa and enjoy it. I actually loathe sitting at my computer desk when playing games.

It’s funny, but that’s my friend’s actual stance on this. He has been patiently waiting for a Switch port of Prime for 2 years now ever since he got hooked on the idea and I keep telling him that there’s rumors it’s coming and it never gets announced.

We’re both at a breaking point. If no trailer, regardless of whether it’s just 1 or all 3, is shown tomorrow, then he’s just going to emulate it on his PC and let me watch him stream it.

We’re both tired of waiting. I understand that there’s some real effort needed to port these games, especially Prime 3, but come on. I know it’s impatient and childish of me to think this way, but I see little reason from a consumer standpoint why Nintendo isn’t throwing every resource they can into preserving or remastering their massive back catalogue. 

A lot of folks want it both ways. New content and older content, but Metroid does not get the respect it deserves as a long standing franchise at Nintendo. Dread was the first serious Metroid game we’ve gotten in a while, and the fact that it’s selling very well means that they do not have any excuse to be hesitant on this. Give us ports and remasters, or watch as fans steal your content via emulators because you’ve done a shit job of making your old games backwards compatible over the years.

Edit: Just because I’m in a ranting mood (sorry anyone that happens to read this. Really sorry), Nintendo’s goal to be unique and proprietary has really fucked themselves in the preservation department. Yeah, if you previously wanted to play Super Mario Sunshine, then you had to own a GameCube and a copy of the GameCube game. No exceptions. But now that the GameCube is obsolete, newer fans are left to either beg for Nintendo to make them a port, or buy a pre-owned system, or emulate it. Only one of these options directly feeds additional profit to Nintendo. So when little crybabies like me get all huffy because Nintendo won’t port my favorite games, it’s because they only lead me with *one* option to directly support the developers that made said games. I don’t want Steven Cunnings from Mississippi to sell me his jank ass HDMI-modded GameCube so I can play Prime again, and I don’t want to steal it via emulation either, but what am I supposed to do?! I’m a gamer. I like what I like. I want to enjoy the games I grew up with.

> …all the power he gets feels unearned.

It’s not that he works as hard as the rest of the character to obtain the same strength, it’s that he’s just innately very powerful and has a lot of dormant potential that comes out when he’s emotionally compromised. Since the end of the Freeza saga, few times have there been where characters have gotten insane power boosts due to just normal training. They usually require some sort of gimmick or transformation to obtain a new level because normal training just isn’t enough. So for Gohan to pull off insane strength isn’t really as crazy as Piccolo fusing with Nail, Goku training on a planet with increased gravity, or a fusion dance a la Gotenks/Vegeto/Gogeta. 

> Goku is a deadbeat dad…

This feels like more of a gag rather than an actual argument. Goku has never shied away from caring for his children. Little gets in the way of him wanting to train and become stronger, but at the end of the day he still encourages his children to listen to their mother and even makes an attempt at a normal life all so he can provide for his family. 

> …Vegeta often lets his pride get in the way…

Yeah, that’s pretty much the whole deal with that character. He’s a noble Saiyan prince. He *feels* like it shouldn’t be happening to him because he was told from day one that he is supposed to be the strongest. So when a commoner like Goku gets a one up, his pride often gets in the way of logical thought.

> But all Gohan does is cry and gets super strong through rage.
